name: Code Review
description: Structured code review process. Reads changes, checks correctness and conventions, and produces a structured verdict. This process is READ-ONLY — it examines code and produces feedback but NEVER modifies anything.
narrative: A review examines a change and judges it; it never edits the code. Read the whole diff first and understand what the change is trying to do, then weigh it on two axes: is it correct (does the logic do what it claims, are the edge cases handled), and is it consistent (naming, patterns, and conventions the rest of the codebase already follows). Close with a clear verdict — approve, approve-with-nits, or request-changes — and make every objection specific enough to act on. Reviewing is read-only: you produce feedback, not commits.
